title: Day 946: Haaretz — Netanyahu's High Court Filing Characterized as Implicit Admission of Oct. 7 Responsibility After 31 Months of Denial
detail: On May 10, 2026 (Day 946 / Ceasefire Day 213), Haaretz published a major analysis piece headlined 'Netanyahu Finally Admits What He Spent 31 Months Denying: Oct. 7 Was on Him,' characterizing the Prime Minister's response to the Supreme Court's petition for a state commission of inquiry as an implicit acknowledgment of personal accountability — a significant break from the public posture Netanyahu maintained since October 7, 2023. For 31 months, Netanyahu had pursued three public 'no's: no personal responsibility, no resignation, and no independent state commission of inquiry with subpoena power over political leadership. His High Court submission, combined with his 55-page response to the state comptroller's investigation that blamed generals (IDF Chief of Staff Herzi Halevi, who resigned in January 2025) and Shin Bet Director Ronen Bar (who resigned March 2025), created a legal framework that placed ultimate governmental responsibility within the executive branch he led. Critics noted the contradiction with his May 8 statement to Israeli media that he is 'solely responsible for Israel's security' — a phrase that, when combined with the mounting evidence from the IDF's own internal probes (including the April 27, 2026 IDF Holit probe finding the community was left undefended for 6 hours 53 minutes), increasingly positioned him as the last major figure who had not formally accepted culpability. Opposition leaders Yair Lapid (Yesh Atid) and Benny Gantz (National Unity) cited the Haaretz analysis to renew calls for a full independent state commission. The October Council (bereaved families' organization) called it 'vindication of two and a half years of struggle' but demanded a formal binding investigation. As of Day 946, 52 days remained until the Supreme Court's July 1, 2026 deadline for the government to present an investigation framework — the most consequential accountability countdown in Israeli democratic history since the Agranat Commission's 1974 findings following the Yom Kippur War.

media.caption: Haaretz May 10, 2026: Netanyahu's High Court filing characterized as implicit Oct. 7 admission after 31 months of denial

title: Day 946: Israel Security Cabinet Convenes to Formally Discuss Gaza War Resumption — IDF Destroys Central Gaza Terror Tunnel as Hamas Holds Firm
detail: On May 10, 2026 (Day 946 / Ceasefire Day 213), Israel's security cabinet convened its most substantive deliberation yet on formally resuming the Gaza war — confirming that operational planning had reached the political authorization threshold. The session, reported by Times of Israel, was directly prompted by Hamas's categorical refusal to engage with the Board of Peace disarmament framework: all four deadlines (April 11, April 14, April 19, and the late-April window) had passed without Hamas compliance, and the Board of Peace's May 6 declaration that it would not hold Israel to ceasefire terms removed the last major international constraint on renewed military operations. On the ground during the cabinet meeting, the IDF was actively destroying a terror tunnel discovered in central Gaza — underscoring that Israeli military operations were already approaching a de facto war resumption threshold. No formal vote to restart full-scale combat operations was publicly announced by day's end; officials indicated the cabinet continued reviewing operational plans for a comprehensive ground offensive against Hamas's remaining military infrastructure. The central constraint remained diplomatic coordination with the Trump administration: Netanyahu was expected to secure explicit US authorization before issuing a formal war resumption order, and the White House's primary regional focus remained the Iran nuclear file. IDF operational readiness for a resumed ground campaign was reported as complete pending political authorization from both Jerusalem and Washington. The security cabinet deliberations also took place against the backdrop of the October 7 investigation deadline — with 52 days remaining until the Supreme Court's July 1 framework requirement, some cabinet members and military analysts raised concerns that a resumed war could further delay accountability proceedings into or beyond Israel's October 2026 general election cycle.

media.caption: Times of Israel: Israeli security cabinet ministers convene to formally discuss Gaza war resumption as Hamas refuses to disarm — Day 946, May 10, 2026
